title: propose_slots holds for decided or pre-interview people, and on every call
body:
## Summary
`proposeSlots` (examples/hirelane/app/actions.ts:225) holds three free interview slots for anyone, at any stage, every time it is called: a rejected or offered candidate, or one still at Applied or Screening, takes slots nobody can book, and a second call holds three more.

## Description
examples/hirelane/app/actions.ts:228 takes `allSlots().filter(isFree).slice(0, 3)` with no stage check and no check for slots already held for this applicant. `sendSchedulingEmail` (same file) refuses with `scheduleReason` unless the person is at Interview and not decided, so slots held for anyone else can never be booked for them until a move - they only lock the calendar. A second call holds three more (six held, nine, ...). The dossier's Propose button reads `actsFor` in examples/hirelane/lib/acts.ts:140, `propose: open(slots.some(isFree) ? null : "no_slot")`, which has the same gap, so the two agree today and both are loose. Fixed looks like: propose refuses `decided` (and `too_early`, the reason `scheduleReason` already names), and tops up to three held slots per person rather than adding three per call - in `lib/acts.ts` (the shared predicate) and the action together. A policy-tighten.

## Flow
- an agent calls `propose_slots` for a rejected applicant -> three free slots go to status 'proposed' for them -> nobody can book those slots for anyone else
- the same agent calls it twice for one applicant -> six slots held
- fix, in build order: add the stage reason to `actsFor().propose` in lib/acts.ts; guard `proposeSlots` with the same reason and REFUSAL sentence; count own held slots and top up to three; rewrite test/acts.test.ts:160's drain loop (it loops `proposeSlots(firstAt("applied"))` and depends on both the pre-interview hold and the re-hold) to drain through several Interview candidates

## Expected impact
A recruiter or an agent loses bookable interview slots to candidates who cannot use them; measured as slots held for decided or pre-interview people after one journey. Could break: the acts parity matrix and the drain loop, which pin today's loose behaviour.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - interview slots are held only for people who can be booked into them, at most three each
Before: proposeSlots succeeds for all 5 stages and holds 3 more slots per call (code read: no stage or own-hold check at app/actions.ts:225-249; lib/acts.ts:140 offers it at every stage)
After: predicted: refused for applied/screening/offer/rejected with the existing REFUSAL sentences; a second call holds 0 new slots
Method: simulation - the round's write set did not include lib/acts.ts (another context's file, the predicate both readers share) and the parity test's drain loop must be rewritten with it; a gate is reachable in a worker that owns both
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
instrument: test/acts.test.ts parity matrix extended with propose for decided and pre-interview applicants (expect refused) and a double-call case (expect 0 new holds); red on the base tree, green after lib/acts.ts + app/actions.ts change

title: L1 carousel ignores the filters the L0 row it was opened from obeys
body:
## Summary
With a filter on, an L0 row says how many people it holds after the filter, but opening it shows the whole unfiltered column: the row reads "2 candidates" and the carousel deals eleven.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/Columns.tsx draws each row from `groupsAt(board, stage, filter)` (components/board/columns/filter.ts), and its aria-label is `Open ${role.title} at ${label}, ${candidates.length} candidates` (Columns.tsx:160) - the filtered count. examples/hirelane/components/board/Board.tsx:468-469 passes the raw `column` to `<Carousel>`, so L1 shows every candidate in that column, and the crumb under it (`shell/Foot.tsx`, `column.candidates.length here`) counts the raw column too. `set_filter`'s own description says "candidates the filter drops leave the board". The tools' `groups()` (components/board/tools/BoardTools.tsx:67) also count unfiltered - another context. Fixed looks like: decide whether L1 obeys the filter (the row's promise) and, if it does, hand the carousel and crumb the filtered column from `columns/filter.ts`, keeping the medians over the whole scored column so the deltas do not move with a filter.

## Flow
- agent calls set_filter {arguable: true} -> the Backend / Screening row reads 2 candidates
- reader opens it -> the carousel deals every Screening candidate, flagged or not; the crumb says 11 here
- fix: a pure `columnFor(board, group, filter)` in columns/filter.ts, read by Board.tsx for the Carousel and the crumb; medians stay on the unfiltered column

## Expected impact
A reader who filtered to the arguable six opens a row and is back among everyone, with no sign the filter stopped applying. Could break: the medians and the carousel's key if the filtered column is a new object per render.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the level a row opens into holds the people the row counted
Before: row count and carousel population agree in 3 of 6 filter combinations on the seed (they disagree whenever arguable-only is on and a column holds unflagged people) - walked from code
After: predicted 6 of 6, by a test over columnFor x the six filter combinations
Method: simulation - the agreement is between a .tsx row label and a .tsx carousel prop; the S-sized pure helper and its test are the instrument, and whether L1 should obey the filter at all is a product reading the worker should confirm against set_filter's description
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/hirelane/components/board/Columns.tsx:160  aria-label={`Open ${role.title} at ${label}, ${candidates.length} candidates`}   (filtered)
examples/hirelane/components/board/Board.tsx:468-469  <Carousel role={role} column={column} ...   (raw column)
examples/hirelane/components/board/tools/BoardTools.tsx:143  set_filter: "candidates the filter drops leave the board"
instrument: test/filter.test.ts: columnFor(board, group, filter).candidates.length equals the L0 row's count for every group and the six filter combinations

title: The masthead headline animates font-size through every level change
body:
## Summary
`.bd-title` transitions `font-size` over `--bd-dur-4` (420ms) when the level changes, which re-lays-out the masthead and moves the stage under the zoom on every frame of the board's signature gesture.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/chrome/mast.css:41 `transition: font-size var(--bd-dur-4) var(--bd-ease), opacity ...`, and `.bd-root[data-level="1"|"2"] .bd-title` drops it from `--bd-text-xl` to `--bd-text-lg`. A font-size transition is layout per frame, it changes the masthead's height (the title is `text-wrap: balance`), and the stage below it is where the 350ms echo is scaling through a measured origin. The repo's motion rule is transform and opacity only in a hot path (overlay config; DESIGN-LAW §1.3), and a level change is the hottest path this surface has. It also runs 70ms longer than the zoom it accompanies (420 vs 350). Fixed looks like: hold the masthead's box still and change the type with a transform (scale from the start edge) or cut the size change at the level boundary under the echo, verified with a layout-shift and frame trace.

## Flow
- reader opens a group (L0 -> L1)
- data-level flips to 1 -> the h1 animates 2 font sizes for 420ms -> each frame re-lays-out the masthead; the stage beneath moves while the echo scales
- reader returns (L1 -> L0) -> the same in reverse

## Expected impact
Every level change pays layout per frame and a moving stage during the signature gesture; measured as layout shifts and long frames in a performance trace of one L0->L1->L0 round trip. Could break: the masthead's wrap at the smaller size if replaced by a transform.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - a level change animates transform and opacity only
Before: 1 layout-property transition on the level-change path (mast.css:41), 420ms against a 350ms zoom - from the stylesheet
After: predicted 0 layout-property transitions on that path; layout shift during the zoom 0
Method: simulation - the cost and the visual alternative can only be measured in a browser (a performance trace of the zoom), which this round does not have
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/chrome/mast.css:41  transition: font-size var(--bd-dur-4) var(--bd-ease), opacity var(--bd-dur-3) var(--bd-ease);
examples/hirelane/components/board/style/chrome/mast.css:49-53  .bd-root[data-level="1"] .bd-title, .bd-root[data-level="2"] .bd-title { font-size: var(--bd-text-lg); opacity: 0.6; }

title: Portrait clipPath ids repeat when one candidate's face is mounted twice
body:
## Summary
`Portrait` names its clipPath `portrait-<candidate id>`, and the same candidate's face is mounted twice whenever the dossier is open over the carousel (and on the board plus its echo during a zoom), so the page carries duplicate ids and `url(#...)` resolves to whichever mounted first.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/marks/Portrait.tsx:56 `const clip = `portrait-${id}``; :68 `<clipPath id={clip}>`; the fill references `url(#${clip})`. At L2 the Carousel stays mounted under the dossier (Board.tsx renders the L1 layer whenever level !== 0), so `carousel/Slide.tsx` and `dossier/Verdict.tsx` both render `<Face size="lg">` for the same candidate; during an L0<->L1 zoom the board and its echo both render the row's faces. Duplicate ids are invalid HTML, and a `url(#id)` that resolves into an element mid-exit or inside a hidden subtree can drop the clip. Fixed looks like: `useId()` for the clip id, which is unique per mount and stable across server and client renders.

## Flow
- reader opens a candidate whose id hashes to a drawn mark (about 3 in 5) -> the slide's face and the dossier's face both emit <clipPath id="portrait-<id>">
- fix: const clip = useId(); keep the rest of the recipe unchanged

## Expected impact
Removes a duplicate-id class from every L2 view and every zoom; measured as duplicate ids in the DOM with the dossier open. Could break: hydration if the id were not useId's.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one DOM id per mounted mark
Before: 2 elements with id portrait-<id> for a drawn candidate with the dossier open (walked from Board.tsx's mount rules)
After: predicted 0 duplicate ids
Method: simulation - counting ids needs a rendered DOM; the package's test runner cannot render .tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/hirelane/components/board/marks/Portrait.tsx:56  const clip = `portrait-${id}`;
examples/hirelane/components/board/marks/Portrait.tsx:68  <clipPath id={clip}>
examples/hirelane/components/board/carousel/Slide.tsx:163  <Face id={candidate.id} ... size="lg" />
examples/hirelane/components/board/dossier/Verdict.tsx:36  <Face id={candidate.id} ... size="lg" />
instrument: a render of Dossier over Carousel (happy-dom + a .tsx loader, see the render-instrument card) counting document.querySelectorAll('[id^=portrait-]') duplicates

title: Closing the note draft or an armed act drops keyboard focus to the document
body:
## Summary
The note draft's Cancel and File it, and every armed act's Cancel and fire, unmount the very button that was pressed, and nothing hands focus to what replaces it, so a keyboard reader is left on <body> inside a modal dialog.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/dossier/Acts.tsx:47-50 `close()` sets `noting` false, which swaps the input row (holding the focused Cancel / File it) for the four act buttons; nothing focuses "Note…" again. examples/hirelane/components/board/dossier/Gate.tsx: Cancel and every fire button call `disarm`, which swaps the armed row for the three arming buttons; the 8-second self-disarm in components/board/useRun.ts (`useArm`) does the same with nobody pressing anything. The dossier's Tab trap (Dossier.tsx onKeyDown) only wraps from first/last, so from <body> the next Tab leaves the dialog for the page behind it. Fixed looks like: return focus to the control that opened the draft or armed the act ("Note…", "Record an offer", ...) when it remounts - a ref per opener and a focus in the effect that follows the swap.

## Flow
- keyboard reader presses Note…, types, presses Cancel -> the row swaps -> document.activeElement is <body>
- keyboard reader arms "Send a rejection", then Cancel -> same
- an armed act self-disarms after 8 s -> focus that was on Cancel goes to <body>
- fix: remember the opener and focus it after the swap

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users lose their place in the dossier after every draft or arming; measured as activeElement after each swap. Could break: focus fighting the dossier's own initial focus if done in the wrong effect.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - focus stays inside the dossier, on the control that opened the closed state
Before: 5 swaps (note Cancel, note File it, arm Cancel x3 kinds, self-disarm) leave focus on <body> - walked from code
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - focus after a React state swap needs a rendered DOM; the runner cannot render .tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a happy-dom render of DossierActs and DossierGate asserting document.activeElement after Cancel, File it and disarm

title: Nineteen board components have no render instrument in the test runner
body:
## Summary
The hirelane test runner is `node --test` with type stripping, which cannot load .tsx, so none of the 19 .tsx files in this context can be rendered in a test; every UI behaviour this round pinned had to be lifted out of source text.

## Description
examples/hirelane/package.json `test` runs `node --import ./test/register.mjs --test "test/**/*.test.ts"`; test/register.mjs resolves aliases and extensionless imports but has no JSX transform and there is no DOM. So focus after a swap, duplicate ids, accessible names and an empty-state render - four of this round's cards - are `simulation` for want of an instrument, and this round's own tests (test/gate.test.ts, test/note.test.ts, test/rail.test.ts) lift handlers out of the .tsx as text. Those work, and they are brittle to a rename. Fixed looks like: a JSX-capable loader hook in test/register.mjs (a transform such as esbuild or sucrase, added as a dev dependency) plus happy-dom, and one smoke test that renders `Dossier` and asserts focus lands on the close button.

## Flow
- add happy-dom and a .tsx transform to test/register.mjs
- render Dossier with a seeded board, assert the close button is focused
- convert test/gate.test.ts and test/note.test.ts to rendered tests; keep the source reads as a fallback

## Expected impact
Turns four UI cards from simulation into gate-decidable items; measured as cards in this context that need a browser to decide. Could break: test start-up time, and the runner's ESM resolution if the loader is ordered wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - UI behaviour in this context is decidable by the package's own test gate
Before: 0 of 19 .tsx files importable by the test runner; 4 cards in this round blocked on it
After: predicted: every .tsx renderable; those 4 cards measurable at the gate rung
Method: probe - `node --import ./test/register.mjs -e "await import('./components/board/dossier/parts.tsx')"` throws ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION; the build itself is a dependency and loader change outside this round's paths (package.json)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/hirelane/package.json:13  "test": "node --import ./test/register.mjs --test \"test/**/*.test.ts\""
examples/hirelane/test/register.mjs:14  const SUFFIXES = [".ts", ".tsx", "/index.ts", "/index.tsx"];  (resolves .tsx, cannot transform it)
instrument: one rendered smoke test (Dossier mounts, close button focused) red before the loader exists, green after

title: presence.ts is a hand-kept copy of ledgerbox's, with no check that the two agree
body:
## Summary
`components/board/presence.ts` says it is "the same file, to the signal, as examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/presence.ts", and it is, line for line in code; nothing keeps it so.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/presence.ts:24 states the contract ("the reading has to mean the same thing in both"); a diff of the two files today differs only in comments. Both decide whether the bridge is present from `window.__athenaBridge` and `detectModelContext()`; a fix to one (say, re-reading when `document.modelContext` appears after mount - today `mc` is captured once and a late-created modelContext never attaches the listener) will land in one app. The kit already owns `detectModelContext` in @athena/demo-kit/webmcp. Fixed looks like: `useAthenaPresence` moves into the kit beside `detectModelContext`, both apps import it, and the two files go.

## Flow
- a reviewer fixes presence.ts in hirelane -> ledgerbox keeps the old reading -> the two tabs of one studio disagree about whether Athena is connected
- fix: move the hook to examples/demo-kit/src/webmcp, re-export, delete both copies

## Expected impact
One reading of "is Athena here" across both apps; measured as copies of the hook (2 -> 1). Could break: the kit's SSR-safety if the hook reads window at import.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one implementation of the presence reading
Before: 2 hand-kept copies, 0 parity checks (diff: code identical, comments differ)
After: predicted 1 implementation in the kit
Method: probe - diffed the two files; the move is outside this round's paths (demo-kit and ledgerbox)
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
$ diff examples/hirelane/components/board/presence.ts examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/presence.ts
(only the header comment differs; imports, interface, NONE and useAthenaPresence are identical)
examples/hirelane/components/board/presence.ts:24  This is the same file, to the signal, as `examples/ledgerbox/components/lanes/presence.ts`.
instrument: a kit test for useAthenaPresence's pure read (bridge string present/absent x modelContext present/absent) plus a grep that no app defines its own

title: Drawn and initials faces announce differently; a slide's name is the whole card
body: ## Summary The two renderings of a face disagree for assistive tech - a drawn mark is `role="img"` titled with the initials, an initials face is `aria-hidden` - and a carousel slide is a `role="option"` button with no label, so its accessible name is every word on the card. ## Description examples/hirelane/components/board/marks/Portrait.tsx:59-60 `{initials}`. So about 3 in 5 candidates are announced with a stray "AK" before their name and the rest are not. examples/hirelane/components/board/carousel/Slide.tsx:129 `role="option"` on a `motion.button` with no aria-label: the option's name is the name, years, headline, overall, fit, band, five criterion rows with their deltas and the stage fact, read as one string each time the listbox moves. Fixed looks like: Portrait `aria-hidden` (the name is always printed beside it), and the slide labelled with what choosing it means (`${name}, ${overall or not scored}, ${fit}`), the rows left as content. ## Flow - screen-reader user arrows along the rail -> each option is read as the entire card, with initials first for drawn faces only - fix: aria-hidden on Portrait's svg; aria-label on Slide from name, overall and fit ## Expected impact The listbox becomes navigable by ear; measured as the accessible name length of an option and its parity across face kinds. Could break: nothing visible. ## Evaluation Claim: user - one accessible name per candidate, short enough to compare by ear Before: face kinds announced differently (2 renderings disagree); option name = the full card text - from code After: predicted: both face kinds silent; option name = name, overall, fit Method: simulation - accessible names need a rendered tree (axe or happy-dom); the runner cannot render .tsx Result: better Gate: none
evidence: examples/hirelane/components/board/marks/Portrait.tsx:59 {initials} examples/hirelane/components/board/carousel/Slide.tsx:129 role="option" (no aria-label on the button)
instrument: axe-core or a happy-dom accessible-name read over a rendered Carousel: one name per option, no initials prefix

title: A group emptied while it is open renders an empty rail captioned as unscored
body:
## Summary
If the last person in an open group leaves it (an agent's move_stage, a decision), L1 stays mounted with zero cards and the caption "nobody here has been scored yet", which describes a different state.

## Description
examples/hirelane/components/board/Board.tsx:146 comes up a level only for `level === 2 && !candidate`. At level 1 a column that has lost its last candidate still has a `role` and a `column`, so the Carousel renders with `ordered = []`: no slides, both arrows disabled, and examples/hirelane/components/board/Carousel.tsx:204 prints "nobody here has been scored yet — the bars stay empty until someone files one" because `column.scored === 0`. L0 hides an empty group entirely (columns/filter.ts drops it), so the level the reader is on describes a group the level above says does not exist. Fixed looks like: extend the orphan rule to `level === 1 && column.candidates.length === 0` (come up to L0, where the row is gone), or give the empty column its own caption.

## Flow
- reader opens a one-person group; an agent moves that person to the next stage
- the page revalidates -> L1 shows no cards and says nobody has been scored yet
- fix: Board.tsx's orphan rule covers an empty column at L1

## Expected impact
A reader watching an agent work is never left on an empty level with a caption about scoring; measured as reachable empty-L1 renders. Could break: the zoom-out echo when the level changes under a flight.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - an emptied group sends the reader back to the board rather than showing a misleading empty rail
Before: 1 reachable state (L1, 0 candidates) rendered with the unscored caption - walked from Board.tsx:146 and Carousel.tsx:204
After: predicted 0
Method: simulation - the state needs a render with a revalidated board; the runner cannot render .tsx
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
examples/hirelane/components/board/Board.tsx:146  const orphaned = level === 2 && !candidate;
examples/hirelane/components/board/Carousel.tsx:204  ? "nobody here has been scored yet — the bars stay empty until someone files one"
instrument: a rendered Board at level 1 re-rendered with the group's column emptied: expect level 0
